endorsements.quote: Surgeons should disclose the use of genAI for surgical decision-making or any other purpose to their patients and in medical notes as they would for any other clinical intervention.
Surgeons should disclose the use of genAI for surgical decision-making or any other purpose to their patients and in medical notes as they would for any other clinical intervention.
Patients should be given AI-generated recommendations and alternative options, ensuring they understand their right to accept or decline AI tools.
Surgeons must transparently discuss the AI’s benefits and limitations, emphasizing that the final decision is always the patients’.
Surgeons should ensure informed consent and prevent overreliance on AI.
To uphold patient autonomy, healthcare providers must prioritize transparency and regular communication about AI’s role and ensure patients understand how their data might be (re)used over time.
Development, trials, and validation should incorporate input from varied backgrounds to enhance transparency in intended use, population limits, and generalizability.
Ensuring equity in surgical genAI requires commitment throughout the so-called algorithm life cycle, starting with diverse and representative data collection.

Unlike static medical tools, genAI models evolve over time, requiring continuous monitoring by developers, investors, and surgeons to maintain quality, implement improvements, and assess potential adverse effects.
Independent review boards with multidisciplinary experts should audit these models for validity.

unlisted_practices: Subject all genAI models to rigorous, plastic surgery-specific testing before clinical use, including simulated surgical scenarios and standard medical device evaluation metrics.
Ensure genAI decisions are reversible and designed to assist, not replace, surgeons.
Ensure AI-generated direct-to-patient communications are accurate, clear, and supplemented by human supervision.
Design genAI tools with usability and seamless integration, with minimal onboarding tutorials, to avoid adding clinician workload.
Have surgeons collaborate with start-ups to provide iterative feedback on genAI tools.
Complement explainable AI with commitments to collect more robust and diverse training data.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/framework paper proposing ethical principles adapted from WHO recommendations to guide the governance and adoption of generative AI in plastic surgery.
